rules.explanation: Professional embedded applications require robust handling of standard hardware communication buses (UART, SPI, I2C, CAN) with error detection.
rules.do: Implement explicit configuration, clock speed setup, and error handling for communication peripherals (e.g., CRC checks, timeout handling).
rules.dont: Do not use blocking polling loops indefinitely without hardware/software timeout mechanisms for peripheral responses.

rules.rule_name: Direct Register Access and Bare-Metal Proficiency
rules.explanation: Demonstrating register-level configuration shows a deep hardware understanding beyond high-level vendor libraries.
rules.do: Document register manipulation (bit-masking, bit-shifting) and register structures for microcontrollers like STM32/AVR.
rules.dont: Do not rely exclusively on auto-generated code tools without understanding the underlying hardware register operations.

rules.explanation: Offloading high-bandwidth data transfers from CPU to DMA improves real-time responsiveness and reduces power consumption.
rules.do: Utilize DMA for serial data transfers and peripheral-to-memory operations where continuous CPU polling is inefficient.
rules.dont: Do not tie up CPU cycles in heavy data transfer loops when hardware DMA channels are available.

rules.rule_name: Hardware Timers and Pulse Width Modulation (PWM)
rules.explanation: Accurate timing, signal generation, and motor control depend on hardware timers rather than software delay routines.
rules.do: Use hardware timer interrupts and hardware PWM generation for precise delays, sampling rates, and actuator control.
rules.dont: Do not use software delay loops (like delay_ms()) for critical timing in multitasking or real-time embedded software.
